title: Sordland/Turn03/PSnW_Overview
description: Ciara Walda and Paskal Beniwoll talk about the overall situation of education and healthcare in the country. They expand each branch in detail and talk about the facts surrounding both. If the player is invested it can acquire more information. The conversation leads to a potential swaying of the player opinion through a debate.

entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Such a spectacular view.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Such a spectacular view.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Ciara Walda, the Minister of Educat..."
entries.dialogueText: Ciara Walda, the Minister of Education, joined us on the balcony, dressed in a sky-blue pantsuit. Her preference for trousers over dresses had made her the subject of much Palace gossip, but it didn't seem to bother her in the slightest.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "While I was mesmerized by the scene..."
entries.dialogueText: While I was mesmerized by the scenery, Paskal Beniwoll walked up to me.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Hopelessness and a lack of opportu..."
entries.dialogueText: “Hopelessness and a lack of opportunities can drive people to extreme solutions. We're seeing increased crime, domestic violence, and yes, rising inequality between men and women..."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“There is another subject I want to..."
entries.dialogueText: “There is another subject I want to mention. I have been working on improving the rights of workers in our country and have proposed a draft bill that is currently being reviewed by our party.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "We headed back inside."
entries.dialogueText: We headed back inside.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The meeting room was already prepar..."
entries.dialogueText: The meeting room was already prepared for state business. Small gifts for each of us had been placed on the table by the municipality. We took our seats.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let's start with your health overv..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's start with your health overview, Paskal.”
entries.menuText: “Let's start with your health overview, Paskal.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Tell me more about your plans, Cia..."
entries.dialogueText: “Tell me more about your plans, Ciara.”
entries.menuText: “Tell me more about your plans, Ciara.”

entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“We have 31,594 doctors and 73,680..."
entries.dialogueText: “We have 31,594 doctors and 73,680 nurses working for the Ministry of Health. This is a high number. What I think is--”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“There are ten beds per ten thousan..."
entries.dialogueText: “There are ten beds per ten thousand citizens. Compared to most of our neighbors, this is a very good number."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Our life expectancy is 65 years. T..."
entries.dialogueText: “Our life expectancy is 65 years. The infant mortality rate is a worrying 121 per one thousand births, while our maternal mortality is at 5 per thousand.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Currently there are about five mil..."
entries.dialogueText: “Currently there are about five million students. Three million in primary education, one million in secondary and one million in tertiary. There are 155,316 teachers.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“The literacy rate of Sordland is a..."
entries.dialogueText: “The literacy rate of Sordland is at eighty percent. This is a very good indicator for future growth, but it needs to increase. It's also far lower among girls than boys.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Urban areas have three times the n..."
entries.dialogueText: “Urban areas have three times the number of schools per ten thousand people compared to rural areas. Rural areas also suffer from a lack of teachers.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“I am doing my best to ensure that..."
entries.dialogueText: “I am doing my best to ensure that citizens of all ages receive the best healthcare they can. I also personally want to solve our high infant and maternal mortality problem.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I don't want to be rude, but out o..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't want to be rude, but out of those numbers. how many are in urban and in rural areas?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Good point, Ciara. Paskal?”"
entries.dialogueText: “Good point, Ciara. Paskal?”
entries.menuText: “Good point, Ciara. Paskal?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let's not interrupt each other, pl..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's not interrupt each other, please.”
entries.menuText: “Let's not interrupt each other.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“That's not a problem. The number o..."
entries.dialogueText: “That's not a problem. The number of doctors per ten thousand citizens is far lower in rural areas compared to urban areas.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“The data shows that per ten thousa..."
entries.dialogueText: “The data shows that per ten thousand people in urban areas there are about eleven doctors, while in rural areas there are only three.”

entries.dialogueText: “My highest priority is to get enough funding to be able to build schools in rural areas while I cleanse our educational system of its nationalistic indoctrination and sexist teachings."

entries.dialogueText: “If I remember correctly, the most illiterate areas are Bergia and Agnland.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“That is correct. Although Lachaven..."
entries.dialogueText: “That is correct. Although Lachaven skews the statistics for the Nargis region, which also has a vast number of illiterate citizens. This underlines my point about the lack of access to education."

entries.dialogueText: “This is one of the most important problems we face, if not the most important. A huge part of the population is forgotten in terms of welfare.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“What is it, Ciara?”"
entries.dialogueText: “What is it, Ciara?”
entries.menuText: “What is it, Ciara?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I hope both of you are preparing y..."
entries.dialogueText: “I hope both of you are preparing your reform plans for improvement.”
entries.menuText: “I hope both of you are preparing your reform plans for improvement.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Look at this impoverished city. Th..."
entries.dialogueText: “Look at this impoverished city. The streets full of potholes, the hospital barely functioning, the school half open.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "She ignored my statement."
entries.dialogueText: She ignored my statement.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“This is not just about Soll or eve..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is not just about Soll or even Alphonso failing. This decay in Sordland's forgotten regions has been going on for many decades due to structural corruption, which is fueled by capitalism.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Paskal, what do you think?”"
entries.dialogueText: “Paskal, what do you think?”
entries.menuText: “Paskal, what do you think?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We are here to change that trend a..."
entries.dialogueText: “We are here to change that trend and to provide for the people.”
entries.menuText: “We are here to change that trend and to provide for the people.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Tarquin Soll did more for the coun..."
entries.dialogueText: “Tarquin Soll did more for the country than any of us.”
entries.menuText: “Tarquin Soll did more for the country than any of us.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“There is not much to be said, sir...."
entries.dialogueText: “There is not much to be said, sir. I agree with Ciara, but it is also Gus Manger's job to improve these areas.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“It's the responsibility of each an..."
entries.dialogueText: “It's the responsibility of each and every one of us.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“That remains to be seen. I'm worki..."
entries.dialogueText: “That remains to be seen. I'm working on the new education system, and your support would be welcome.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Really? I must agree to disagree t..."
entries.dialogueText: “Really? I must agree to disagree then.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Did we cover all the necessary sub..."
entries.dialogueText: “Did we cover all the necessary subjects?”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I do hope we won't repeat the same..."
entries.dialogueText: “I do hope we won't repeat the same mistakes again and again. Have a good day, Mr. President.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The ministers left, and I prepared..."
entries.dialogueText: The ministers left, and I prepared to leave for other official business in the city. The Gasom meeting was just one of the many events I was scheduled to attend over the next few days.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "By looking at the citizens’ attire,..."
entries.dialogueText: By looking at the citizens’ attire, it was easy to understand the current state of Narbel. Some people were wearing clothes a few sizes too large. Some kids did not even have shoes. Yet there was hope in their eyes.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: GameCondition.Turn03_PSnW_Overview = true

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“My plans require an increase in th..."
entries.dialogueText: “My plans require an increase in the government budget. I aim to solve the problems we highlighted with the allocated money.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“By building schools in these less..."
entries.dialogueText: “By building schools in these less fortunate rural areas and through fundamental changes to the education system, I will unlock the potential of all our children. Boys and girls alike."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Interesting. I thought our problem..."
entries.dialogueText: "Interesting. I thought our problem was with the quality of education in Sordland as a whole.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Improving the situation in rural a..."
entries.dialogueText: “Improving the situation in rural areas is indeed a good idea.”
entries.menuText: “Improving the situation in rural areas is indeed a good idea.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“It's an investment in the future o..."
entries.dialogueText: “It's an investment in the future of Sordland. Imagine unlocking the full, untapped potential of our youth. The knowledge and wealth they will generate.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Our statistics show the disparity..."
entries.dialogueText: “Our statistics show the disparity between urban and rural education. We can either do something about it, or wait until things get worse.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Wouldn't a promotion of private ed..."
entries.dialogueText: “Wouldn't a promotion of private education help create additional funds?”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Yes, but at what cost? I'm not a s..."
entries.dialogueText: “Yes, but at what cost? I'm not a supporter of the private sector in education. At the end of the day, they are focused on profit first.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“What are you working towards, Pask..."
entries.dialogueText: “What are you working towards, Paskal?”
entries.menuText: “What are you working towards, Paskal?”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“I personally want to improve the l..."
entries.dialogueText: “I personally want to improve the low quality of healthcare in the rural areas.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“I can do more with an increased bu..."
entries.dialogueText: “I can do more with an increased budget. Additionally, a privatization plan to promote private investments in the healthcare system could allocate extra funds.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Isn't access to healthcare in rura..."
entries.dialogueText: “Isn't access to healthcare in rural areas an issue?”
entries.menuText: “Isn't access to healthcare in rural areas an issue?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Improving the quality of healthcar..."
entries.dialogueText: “Improving the quality of healthcare in less fortunate areas should be our highest priority.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Access is an issue, but not as cri..."
entries.dialogueText: “Access is an issue, but not as critical as improving the quality in these areas. The lack of experienced personnel and equipment causes poor treatment, resulting in many deaths.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Exactly. It would directly diminis..."
entries.dialogueText: “Exactly. It would directly diminish our depressingly high infant and maternal mortality situation. Besides, such a push would also have economic benefits.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Lileas Graf will take care of crim..."
entries.dialogueText: “Lileas Graf will take care of crime. She's an expert on the subject."
entries.menuText: “Lileas Graf will take care of crime. She's an expert on the subject."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Those issues must be tackled from..."
entries.dialogueText: “Those issues must be tackled from different directions. We need to engage it holistically.”
entries.menuText: “Those issues must be tackled from different directions. We need to engage it holistically.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“If only we could stop the recessio..."
entries.dialogueText: “If only we could stop the recession, create jobs and growth...”
entries.menuText: “If only we could stop the recession, create jobs and growth...”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“I'm planning to help by using an i..."
entries.dialogueText: “I'm planning to help by using an increased budget to improve the quality of healthcare.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“She is certainly a proven administ..."
entries.dialogueText: “She is certainly a proven administrator. From what I heard she reduced crime in Arvory by 40% during her mayoral term.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“The economic situation does play a..."
entries.dialogueText: “The economic situation does play a huge role in living standards. Our urban and rural disparities are stark, and the recession hit the weakest harder.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I don't think brute force will get..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't think brute force will get us anywhere. Look at where the tight grip of Tarquin Soll got us.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""That could prove useful, but we ne..."
entries.dialogueText: "That could prove useful, but we need to be doing a lot more. Education has similar issues.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“We can't fix the economy by oursel..."
entries.dialogueText: “We can't fix the economy by ourselves. We have to educate the people and let them create new opportunities too.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Agnolia and Wehlen should hardly b..."
entries.dialogueText: “Agnolia and Wehlen should hardly be used as a standard, but it is good to know we aren't in a massive health crisis. Yet.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I think there needs to be a change..."
entries.dialogueText: “I think there needs to be a change in what is being taught. We should help children to ask questions and educate themselves.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Ciara sat back down and sighed."
entries.dialogueText: Ciara sat back down and sighed.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“One way or another, we need change..."
entries.dialogueText: “One way or another, we need change in Sordland. Greed and unchecked capitalism will not magically provide for the people.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Tell me more about your plans, Cia..."
entries.dialogueText: “Tell me more about your plans, Ciara.”
entries.menuText: “Tell me more about your plans, Ciara.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“My expectation from our government..."
entries.dialogueText: “My expectation from our government is that we understand and focus on the needs of the people.”

entries.dialogueText: “Sordish education is free, but we have a very outdated system that I want to reform. The other important issue is the lack of access to education in rural areas, especially for young girls. Your administration has the power to solve both problems."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Sordland has a free healthcare sys..."
entries.dialogueText: “Sordland has a free healthcare system, except for a few private hospitals operating under it. Most of the populace receives adequate treatment. Health issues primarily appear in rural areas due to a lack of quality services.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“As you wish, Mr. President.”"
entries.dialogueText: “As you wish, Mr. President.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“I do hope to create competition an..."
entries.dialogueText: “I do hope to create competition and increase the quality of healthcare with the privatization effort.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“But you must realize that privatiz..."
entries.dialogueText: “But you must realize that privatizing our health care system would increase the price of treatment and make access worse for the average citizen.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Salaries for teachers are very low..."
entries.dialogueText: “Salaries for teachers are very low here. We need to increase their pay to give them more incentive."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“So, I created draft plans to incre..."
entries.dialogueText: “So, I created draft plans to increase the salary of doctors and to upgrade the equipment of the hospitals.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I am glad we see eye to eye on the..."
entries.dialogueText: “I am glad we see eye to eye on the issue.”

entries.speaker: Player

entries.title: Player: "“We knew less fortunate families, e..."
entries.dialogueText: “We knew less fortunate families, even though we belonged to the middle class ourselves.”
entries.menuText: “We knew less fortunate families, even though we belonged to the middle class ourselves.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Thankfully, we never had any probl..."
entries.dialogueText: “Thankfully, we never had any problems with money.”
entries.menuText: "Thankfully, we never had any problems with money.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“So, you could at least sympathize..."
entries.dialogueText: “So, you could at least sympathize with the plight of these people.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“You don't have to have been born p..."
entries.dialogueText: “You don't have to have been born poor to sympathize with the plight of the impoverished. Much as you don't have to have been born a woman to recognize Sordland's need for parity among the sexes.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“You know the saying; you don't kno..."
entries.dialogueText: “You know the saying; you don't know what you have until it is taken from you.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Exactly. It feels as if there is n..."
entries.dialogueText: “Exactly. It feels as if there is no way out.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“It feels like the cards are stacke..."
entries.dialogueText: “It feels like the cards are stacked against you.”
entries.menuText: “It feels like the cards are stacked against you.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“True but some lives are more diffi..."
entries.dialogueText: “True but some lives are more difficult than others. Like ours was, and still is for hundreds of thousands in Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We have all gone through difficult..."
entries.dialogueText: “We have all gone through difficult times.”
entries.menuText: “We have all gone through difficult times.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“As I was saying -- isn't it about..."
entries.dialogueText: “As I was saying -- isn't it about time Holsord addressed this country's real issues? Rather than bowing to the wishes of the hawks and fearmongerers in the establishment, and diverting yet more resources to the military and law enforcement?”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Our welfare, healthcare and educat..."
entries.dialogueText: “Our welfare, healthcare and education systems have been decaying since the recession. Sordland's poorer communities are losing hope."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Sordland needs more schools full o..."
entries.dialogueText: “Sordland needs more schools full of children instead of barracks full of soldiers, more hospitals instead of police stations.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The capital must be prioritised to..."
entries.dialogueText: “The capital must be prioritised towards the resources that matter the most.”
entries.menuText: “The capital must be prioritised towards the resources that matter the most.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“In other words, rural citizens wit..."
entries.dialogueText: “In other words, rural citizens with medical emergencies have to wait an embarassingly long time before they are treated.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“One cannot be separated from the o..."
entries.dialogueText: “One cannot be separated from the other, Mr. Rayne. The issues stem from the ideology."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let's not get into an ideological..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's not get into an ideological debate. We need to focus on the issues.”

entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Besides, it wouldn't fit into the..."
entries.dialogueText: “Besides, it wouldn't fit into the planned economy President Rayne has decided to promote.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“The decision not to promote more s..."
entries.dialogueText: “The decision not to promote more state control would cost the Sordish people dearly.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“I don't want to sound cynical, but..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't want to sound cynical, but almost all governments keep making the same promises. We must show we are different through our actions.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“It is the same play and the same b..."
entries.dialogueText: “It is the same play and the same book. The security complex in the country keeps driving the agenda as usual.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We are elected representatives of..."
entries.dialogueText: “We are elected representatives of our people and we will prioritize their needs.”
entries.menuText: “We are elected representatives of our people and we will prioritize their needs.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“There are other significant issues..."
entries.dialogueText: “There are other significant issues that we need to focus on, like security.”
entries.menuText: “There are other significant issues that we need to focus on, like security.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I appreciate your briefings and pl..."
entries.dialogueText: “I appreciate your briefings and plans. We will re-convene at the budget meeting.”
entries.menuText: “I appreciate your briefings and plans. We will re-convene at the budget meeting.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“That's reassuring to hear.”"
entries.dialogueText: “That's reassuring to hear.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“There have been a lot of negative..."
entries.dialogueText: “There have been a lot of negative developments lately.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“It was a pleasure.”"
entries.dialogueText: “It was a pleasure.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“See you at the meeting. I hope to..."
entries.dialogueText: “See you at the meeting. I hope to see a change in direction.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Spectacular indeed. But if you loo..."
entries.dialogueText: “Spectacular indeed. But if you look in the opposite direction, you will see what Soll's decades of neglect did to the city.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I arrived at the meeting room for m..."
entries.dialogueText: I arrived at the meeting room for my talk with Ciara and Paskal. Before beginning, I took a moment to appreciate the view from the balcony. The mountains of Narbel were completely covered with snow.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Whatever. I'd much rather be in Ho..."
entries.dialogueText: “Whatever. I'd much rather be in Holsord right now.”
entries.menuText: “Whatever. I'd much rather be in Holsord right now.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Our presence here will show that w..."
entries.dialogueText: “Our presence here will show that we still remember Narbel and other forgotten areas of our country.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Most of the people living in Narbe..."
entries.dialogueText: “Most of the people living in Narbel are workers, farmers and their wives and children. They're breaking their backs for close to no pay, all thanks to greedy corporations.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“It is important for the people.”"
entries.dialogueText: “It is important for the people.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Real problems like poverty.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Real problems like poverty.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We can't really blame the companie..."
entries.dialogueText: “We can't really blame the companies. That's just how they work.”
entries.menuText: “We can't really blame the companies. That's just how they work.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Yes we can. Similar companies are..."
entries.dialogueText: “Yes we can. Similar companies are doing much better for their workers in United Contana and Arcasia.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "As I made my way out, the weather w..."
entries.dialogueText: As I made my way out, the weather was noticeably cold, but it didn’t keep a group of USP supporters from coming out to cheer us on the streets.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "They were excited to see their pres..."
entries.dialogueText: They were excited to see their president in their city.

entries.dialogueText: “I personally promised that our health systems were to be improved in our term. I fully support you, Paskal.”
entries.menuText: “I personally promised that our health systems were to be improved in our term. I fully support you Paskal.”

entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Exactly. Increasing law enforcemen..."

entries.dialogueText: “The people will rejoice if they see grand improvements in welfare. Our public opinion ratings will increase drastically.”

entries.dialogueText: “It's getting a little cold out here. Shall we continue our discussion indoors?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I agree. We need to improve the st..."
entries.dialogueText: “I agree. We need to improve the standards for our workers.”
entries.menuText: “I agree. We need to improve the standards for our workers.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Mr. Clavin has already backed me a..."
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. Clavin has already backed me and given his support. Sordland has fallen behind most countries on this subject and it is my responsibility to ensure this is not the case.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“There is always room for improveme..."
entries.dialogueText: “There is always room for improvement and it is good to hear that you are pushing for it.”
entries.menuText: “There is always room for improvement and it is good to hear that you are pushing for it.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We shouldn't upset the businesses..."
entries.dialogueText: “We shouldn't upset the businesses who are already struggling to stay afloat in the crisis.”
entries.menuText: “We shouldn't upset the businesses who are already struggling to stay afloat in the crisis.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“It also is a matter of life and de..."
entries.dialogueText: “It also is a matter of life and death. Every decade we hear of some horrific accident due to employers' disregard for their workers' safety."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Exactly. Sordland must provide for..."
entries.dialogueText: “Exactly. Sordland must provide for its own people to move forward.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Appreciate the kind words, Mr. Pre..."
entries.dialogueText: “Appreciate the kind words, Mr. President. I will not let you down.”

entries.dialogueText: “Why would you turn away from the pro-labor cause when you yourself supported the Red Youth during your university years?”

entries.dialogueText: “This wouldn't alter the balance of operational companies drastically. It would just punish them if they are treating their workers unfairly.”

entries.title: Player: "“Thank you, Paskal. Your in-depth b..."
entries.dialogueText: “Thank you, Paskal. Your in-depth briefing is much appreciated.”
entries.menuText: “Thank you, Paskal. Your in-depth briefing is much appreciated.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Thank you, Ciara. I can fill in th..."
entries.dialogueText: “Thank you, Ciara. I can fill in the blanks from here.”
entries.menuText: “Thank you, Ciara. I can fill in the blanks from here.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“Parity among the sexes shouldn't b..."
entries.dialogueText: “Parity among the sexes shouldn't be our first priority. Look at how many high-ranking female politicians our country has."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""Appearances can be deceiving, Pask..."
entries.dialogueText: "Appearances can be deceiving, Paskal."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Her voice sounded bitter."
entries.dialogueText: Her voice sounded bitter.

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""Think about how Lileas Graf got to..."
entries.dialogueText: "Think about how Lileas Graf got to her current position. I don't necessarily believe the rumors about her and Soll, but she never could have risen so high if she didn't parrot his cause."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""Gloria Tory -- is it an accident t..."
entries.dialogueText: "Gloria Tory -- is it an accident that the first female Assembly speaker is such a staunch conservative?"

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""And then there was Alphonso's habi..."
entries.dialogueText: "And then there was Alphonso's habit of promoting women to prominent positions to give Sordland a progressive sheen while accomplishing nothing in reality..."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""While women in places like Narbel..."
entries.dialogueText: "While women in places like Narbel are denied any opportunity to advance, the government can use a handful of female politicians from wealthy families -- myself included -- to pretend their only obstacle to success is their own lack of initiative."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""Meanwhile, those of us who don't u..."
entries.dialogueText: "Meanwhile, those of us who don't use our clout to help powerful men stay in power are denigrated as angry spinsters... I ask you, Mr. President, does anyone care that your strategist Mr. Galade doesn't have a wife?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I've been wondering about that, ac..."
entries.dialogueText: "I've been wondering about that, actually."
entries.menuText: "I've been wondering about that, actually."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Leave Lucian out of this.""
entries.dialogueText: "Leave Lucian out of this."
entries.menuText: "Leave Lucian out of this."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""You've veered off-topic, Ms. Walda.""
entries.dialogueText: "You've veered off-topic, Ms. Walda."
entries.menuText: "You've veered off-topic, Ms. Walda."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I agree with you completely. Sordl..."
entries.dialogueText: "I agree with you completely. Sordland's women deserve better."
entries.menuText: "I agree with you completely. Sordland's women deserve better."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""Mr. Beniwoll asked. I answered.""
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. Beniwoll asked. I answered."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: ""All right, Ciara. You've made your..."
entries.dialogueText: "All right, Ciara. You've made your point."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""I'm glad to hear that.""
entries.dialogueText: "I'm glad to hear that."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: ""Nevertheless, it's worth acknowled..."
entries.dialogueText: "Nevertheless, it's worth acknowledging the corporation's significant contribution to job creation in Narbel and other poverty-stricken regions. Persuading the chairman to make concessions might prove to be a formidable task."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: ""One more thing. I wish to raise my..."
entries.dialogueText: "One more thing. I wish to raise my concerns about your scheduled meeting with the Gasom chairman and former President, Mr. Alphonso."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""What is there to negotiate, Paskal..."
entries.dialogueText: "What is there to negotiate, Paskal? The standards for Gasom workers are already at rock bottom. President Rayne can and must demand better."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""What good is job creation if the w..."
entries.dialogueText: "What good is job creation if the workers are treated poorly? Of course I'll demand better from Alphonso."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I know how slippery Alphonso can b..."
entries.dialogueText: "I know how slippery Alphonso can be. Bringing this up with him will indeed be a challenge."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""If we do this right, we can find a..."
entries.dialogueText: "If we do this right, we can find a solution that advances both the economy and the interests of laborers."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: ""I covered this topic extensively i..."
entries.dialogueText: "I covered this topic extensively in one of my books. Confrontation, if not handled prudently, could exacerbate the challenges these workers face."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: ""Try a diplomatic approach. Deep do..."
entries.dialogueText: "Try a diplomatic approach. Deep down, I believe he wants what is best for the workers as well."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: ""That would be quite the impressive..."
entries.dialogueText: "That would be quite the impressive feat. You'd make headlines for it."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“This matter is close to my heart...."
entries.dialogueText: “This matter is close to my heart. I would personally be grateful if you are able to resolve the concerns raised by Katarina Horten and her fellow labor representatives.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“It would be difficult to imagine a..."
entries.dialogueText: “It would be difficult to imagine a CEO like Alphonso giving benefits to workers without him personally gaining from it.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""In this world, nothing is truly fr..."
entries.dialogueText: "In this world, nothing is truly free. I wouldn't anticipate anything less."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Gasom relies on us just as we rely..."
entries.dialogueText: "Gasom relies on us just as we rely on them. We can find a path to compromise."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Gasom has profited from the labor..."
entries.dialogueText: "Gasom has profited from the labor of workers for far too long. It's time for them to give back."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“We must be cautious about these se..."
entries.dialogueText: “We must be cautious about these seemingly generous offers. They usually come with hidden costs that further tip the scales in favor of the privileged few.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“The middle way often sways perilou..."
entries.dialogueText: “The middle way often sways perilously close to the status quo. We must ensure that any negotiations genuinely benefit the people and not just uphold the interests of corporate giants.”

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“We shouldn't settle for anything l..."
entries.dialogueText: “We shouldn't settle for anything less than a complete overhaul of the exploitative structures Gasom and its fellow corporations have built.”

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: ""Thank you for your input, Ciara. B..."
entries.dialogueText: "Thank you for your input, Ciara. But I will stress to President Rayne how important it is that the door to dialogue remain open."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: ""Ideology should never get in the w..."
entries.dialogueText: "Ideology should never get in the way of bringing about tangible, lasting change."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: ""By negotiating with Alphonso and h..."
entries.dialogueText: "By negotiating with Alphonso and his company, you have an opportunity to secure better labor conditions for blue-collar Gasom employees. This could be a triumph for all of Narbel."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""My foremost priorities lie in impr..."
entries.dialogueText: "My foremost priorities lie in improving the economy. Once that is achieved, upward mobility will naturally follow suit."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: ""Economic improvements don't always..."
entries.dialogueText: "Economic improvements don't always automatically translate into greater happiness and well-being, Mr. President."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Considering our need for greater e..."
entries.dialogueText: "Considering our need for greater energy security, we might find ourselves forced to collaborate with him."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: ""Remember, these 'collaborations' u..."
entries.dialogueText: "Remember, these 'collaborations' usually come with strings attached. Often, they disproportionately favor corporations while placing the burden on the common people."

entries.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
entries.title: Paskal Beniwoll: "“We shall keep you no longer. Thank..."
entries.dialogueText: “We shall keep you no longer. Thank you both for the discussions."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I'm encouraged by the willingness..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm encouraged by the willingness of Mr. Manger and Mr. Alphonso to meet with me. It's a step forward."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I disagree. Only by holding firm t..."
entries.dialogueText: "I disagree. Only by holding firm to my convictions can I bring about the change Sordland needs."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I'm skeptical that these discussio..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm skeptical that these discussions with Gasom will lead to any meaningful change. We've seen empty promises before."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I can't promise anything to either..."
entries.dialogueText: "I can't promise anything to either of you. I've got to get a grasp of the situation at Gasom first."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""No need for the briefing, I'm up t..."
entries.dialogueText: "No need for the briefing, I'm up to speed."
entries.menuText: "No need for the briefing, I'm up to speed."

entries.speaker: Ciara Walda
entries.title: Ciara Walda: "“Oh, okay.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Oh, okay.”
